### A boundary-safe parabolic symmetrizer

Put \(D(c)=M(c)^{-1}\)\. For every \(c\in\Sigma_N\), define the matrix \(P(c)\) by

\[
\boxed{D(c)^\top P(c)+P(c)D(c)=2I_d.}
\tag{4}
\]

Because all eigenvalues of \(D(c)\) have positive real parts, this Lyapunov equation has a unique symmetric positive-definite solution, explicitly

\[
P(c)=2\int_0^\infty
e^{-D(c)^\top r}e^{-D(c)r}\,dr.
\]

The integral is only a proof representation. The matrix \(P(c)\) is computable algebraically by solving the finite linear system (4), using the Kronecker-sum matrix.

Thus \(P(c)\) is rational in the concentration variables, smooth on a neighborhood of \(\Sigma_N\), and

\[
\boxed{
P(c)D(c)+D(c)^\top P(c)=2I_d.
}
\]

Unlike the logarithmic entropy Hessian, this symmetrizer remains finite at zero concentrations.

It supplies a uniformly coercive principal quadratic form for local quasilinear-parabolic estimates, with constants depending only on \(N\) and the friction array.

**What it establishes\:** Normal ellipticity and boundary-safe local strong solvability do not require the special Stieltjes coordinate structure. The missing global result is an a priori regularity estimate, not algebraic invertibility of the Maxwell–Stefan flux law.
